results.claim: His published client sent our paired-write fixture over real HTTP and it behaved as he reported.
Under his own PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL a DELETE leaves every copy of the payload in the -wal sidecar file.
A VACUUM does not remove the deleted payload from the -wal file.
A wal_checkpoint TRUNCATE on its own moves the deleted payload into the durable database file.
Only a VACUUM and a checkpoint together clear the payload from both files, and secure_delete ON also clears it.
His _claim selects only rows in state pending, so a delivered row is never resent by his client.
The retention of a delivered row is what lets his enqueue refuse a changed payload under an existing source id offline.
Our deletion manifest never registered his outbox as an erasure target, although his README says retention belongs to the caller.
His freeze_record copies the raw source dict into writer_metadata, so a doc identifier reaches his receiver intact today.
Writing a channel and principal source back into inspeximus fails because our own _check_source demands a doc key.
When a source carries both doc and principal his _normal_source keeps principal and drops the doc value while the channel still reads doc.
Our erasure_v0 file carries three operations where schema_v0 has one, superseded, retracted and erased.
The two proposed endpoints are POST /mnemo/v0/erase and POST /mnemo/v0/still_recoverable.
Under GDPR Article 17(3)(b) a controller under a retention duty can lawfully refuse to erase, to the extent that duty reaches.
The schema_v0 id was a 404 because we renamed a folder on 21 July, which is seven weeks ago, and it is now fixed.
